purpose: Codeine is used to relieve mild to moderate pain that is not controlled by regular pain relievers like ibuprofen or acetaminophen alone. It is also used to help reduce a dry, bothersome cough. Sometimes it is combined with other medicines like acetaminophen for extra pain relief.
how_it_works: Codeine belongs to a group of medicines called opioids. Once you take it, your body converts it into morphine, which then attaches to special receptors in your brain and spinal cord that control pain and coughing. This blocks pain signals and calms the cough reflex, helping you feel more comfortable.
common_side_effects: The most common side effects include constipation, nausea, drowsiness, dizziness, and lightheadedness. Some people may feel itchy or have an upset stomach. Taking it with food can help reduce stomach upset.
warnings: Codeine can be habit-forming, so it is important to take only the amount prescribed and not for longer than directed. Do not drink alcohol while taking codeine as it can cause dangerous drowsiness. Codeine should NOT be given to children under 12, and it is not recommended for teenagers after certain surgeries like tonsil removal. Some people are ultra-rapid metabolizers, meaning their body converts codeine to morphine very fast, which can be dangerous. Tell your doctor about all your medications to avoid harmful interactions.
typical_dosing: For adults, the usual dose for pain is 15 to 60 mg every 4 to 6 hours as needed. For cough, a typical dose is 10 to 20 mg every 4 to 6 hours. Never take more than 360 mg in one day. Always follow exactly what your doctor or pharmacist tells you.
